product_overview: ScrapyCoco is a web-based administration dashboard for managing and monitoring football data scrapers. It lets users run scrapers, watch live logs, review history and metrics, schedule automated runs, export data, and inspect scraper HTML diagnostics from a single interface.
core_goals: View the available scrapers and their current status
Run individual scrapers or multiple scrapers in sequence
Monitor live execution logs while scrapers run
Review execution history and performance metrics
Export scraped data in common file formats
Inspect HTML diagnostics to support scraper maintenance

features.name: Scraper Grid
features.description: Lets users view the available scrapers as cards, inspect their status and last run, select multiple scrapers, and launch individual runs or previews.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> View all scraper cards -> Inspect each scraper’s status and last run -> Select a scraper -> Run the scraper -> See live execution output and completion state
Navigate to / -> View all scraper cards -> Inspect each scraper’s status and last run -> Select a scraper -> Open the data preview -> See the scraped data preview
Navigate to / -> View all scraper cards -> Select multiple scrapers -> Start batch execution -> See progress updates and completion summary

features.name: Live Terminal Logs
features.description: Shows real-time scraper output in a terminal-style widget with log filtering, clearing, and autoscroll controls.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Start a scraper run -> Watch streaming log lines appear in the terminal -> See the run progress in real time -> See the final completion message
Navigate to / -> Start a scraper run -> Change the log level filter -> See only matching log lines remain visible
Navigate to / -> Start a scraper run -> Clear the terminal output -> See the console reset -> Toggle autoscroll on or off

features.name: History Dashboard
features.description: Provides a history view of past scraper executions along with summary metrics and charts.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open the Historial tab -> View the execution history table -> Inspect dates, durations, and statuses for past runs
Navigate to / -> Open the Historial tab -> Filter history by scraper -> See the table update to matching runs only
Navigate to / -> Open the Historial tab -> View the success and failure chart -> View the average duration chart -> Review global totals, success rate, and average duration

features.name: Scheduler Management
features.description: Allows users to review scheduled scraper tasks and manage them through add, pause, resume, delete, and immediate run actions.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open the Programador tab -> View the list of scheduled tasks -> Add a new task with a cron schedule -> See the task appear in the list
Navigate to / -> Open the Programador tab -> Select an existing task -> Pause the task -> See its state change to paused -> Resume the task -> See its state change back to active
Navigate to / -> Open the Programador tab -> Select an existing task -> Delete the task -> See it removed from the list
Navigate to / -> Open the Programador tab -> Select an existing task -> Run the task immediately -> See the execution begin

features.name: Data Export
features.description: Lets users export scraped data in CSV, JSON, or Excel formats with optional transformations.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open the Configuración tab -> Select a scraper for export -> Choose an export format -> Apply optional transforms -> Download the exported file
Navigate to / -> Open the Configuración tab -> Select a scraper for export -> Choose a different export format -> Download the exported file

features.name: HTML Diagnostic
features.description: Provides HTML structure analysis tools for scraper maintenance, including diagnostic snapshots and comparisons.
user_flows: Navigate to / -> Open a scraper card’s diagnostic action -> Run the HTML diagnostic -> View the structure analysis results
Navigate to / -> Open a scraper card’s diagnostic action -> View diagnostic history snapshots -> Compare two snapshots -> See the differences between them

routes.description: Single-page dashboard with 4 tabs (Extraction, History, Config, Scheduler)

features.name: Scraper Grid
features.description: Display 8 scrapers as interactive cards with status, last run, and action buttons
user_interactions: View all 8 scraper cards with names and descriptions
Select scrapers via checkboxes for batch execution
Click "Vista Previa" to see scraped data preview

features.name: Batch Execution
features.description: Select and run multiple scrapers sequentially with progress bar
user_interactions: See progress bar updating in real-time
View logs from each scraper in the terminal

features.name: Live Terminal Logs
features.description: Real-time console output from running scrapers via SSE
user_interactions: View streaming log lines in terminal widget

features.name: History Dashboard
features.description: View execution history with charts and metrics
user_interactions: View execution history table with dates and statuses
See bar chart (average duration per scraper)
View global stats (total runs, success rate, avg duration)

features.name: Scheduler Management
features.description: CRUD operations for automated scraper scheduling
user_interactions: Add new scheduled task with cron expression
Click "Run Now" to execute task immediately

features.name: Data Export
features.description: Export scraped data as CSV, JSON, or Excel

features.name: HTML Diagnostic
features.description: Analyze HTML structure of target websites for scraper maintenance
user_interactions: Click diagnostic button on a scraper card

known_limitations.issue: Preview and export only supported for class-based scrapers (FBref, Flashscore, Transfermarkt), not for legacy scripts (results, wc2026, elo)
known_limitations.impact: Script-based scrapers cannot preview or export data through the UI
